skills: Vertex, axis of symmetry and intercepts
Polynomial behaviour and the remainder theorem

lesson.intro: Topic 7 asked you to \emph{solve} a quadratic equation. This topic asks something different: given a quadratic or polynomial \emph{function}, what does its graph look like, and which algebraic form of the rule shows you that? The Digital SAT tests this constantly, and almost always in the same three ways: read a feature (vertex, intercept, axis of symmetry) off a form that already displays it; rewrite the rule into the form that displays the feature you want; or reason about a higher-degree polynomial from its factors. A question such as ``which of the following equivalent forms displays the minimum value as a constant or coefficient?'' is not asking you to compute anything at all -- it is asking whether you know what each form shows.

blocks.title: The three forms of a parabola
blocks.body:
Every quadratic function can be written in three ways, and all three describe the same curve. What changes is which feature is visible without doing any work.

\textbf{Standard form} $f(x)=ax^2+bx+c$ shows the $y$-intercept: putting $x=0$ leaves $f(0)=c$, so the graph crosses the $y$-axis at $(0,c)$.

\textbf{Vertex form} $f(x)=a(x-h)^2+k$ shows the vertex $(h,k)$ and therefore the axis of symmetry $x=h$ and the maximum or minimum value $k$.

\textbf{Factored form} $f(x)=a(x-r)(x-s)$ shows the $x$-intercepts $(r,0)$ and $(s,0)$, the values of $x$ that make the output zero.

In all three, the sign of $a$ decides the direction: $a>0$ opens upward and the vertex is a minimum, $a<0$ opens downward and the vertex is a maximum.

blocks.title: The facts to have automatic
blocks.body:
\textbf{Axis of symmetry / vertex $x$-coordinate from standard form:}
\[ x=-\frac{b}{2a} \]
\textbf{Vertex $y$-coordinate:} substitute that $x$ back into the function -- $f\!\left(-\frac{b}{2a}\right)$ is the maximum or minimum value.

\textbf{Midpoint shortcut:} if the graph crosses the $x$-axis at $x=r$ and $x=s$, the axis of symmetry is exactly halfway between them, $x=\dfrac{r+s}{2}$.

\textbf{Vertex form:} $f(x)=a(x-h)^2+k$ has vertex $(h,k)$.

\textbf{$y$-intercept, always:} evaluate $f(0)$, whatever the form.

blocks.title: Match the question to the form
blocks.body:
When a question names a feature, it is telling you which form to move toward.
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=14pt,itemsep=2pt,topsep=2pt]
  \item ``vertex'', ``maximum'', ``minimum'', ``axis of symmetry'' $\Rightarrow$ vertex form, or $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$.
  \item ``$x$-intercepts'', ``zeros'', ``solutions'', ``where the graph meets the $x$-axis'' $\Rightarrow$ factored form.
  \item ``$y$-intercept'', ``initial value'', ``value when $x=0$'' $\Rightarrow$ standard form, or just substitute $0$.
\end{itemize}
Nothing about the parabola changes when you rewrite it. Only your view of it does.

blocks.title: Completing the square: standard form to vertex form
blocks.body: To rewrite $ax^2+bx+c$ in vertex form, factor $a$ out of the first two terms, add and subtract the square of half the resulting linear coefficient, and tidy up. On the SAT you can almost always skip the algebra: compute $h=-\frac{b}{2a}$, compute $k=f(h)$, and write $a(x-h)^2+k$. That takes two substitutions and is far harder to botch than completing the square under time pressure.

blocks.title: Worked example 1 -- rewriting to show the minimum
blocks.body:
\textbf{Which of the following is equivalent to $f(x)=2x^2-12x+13$ and displays the minimum value of $f$ as a constant or coefficient?}

The phrase ``minimum value \dots\ as a constant'' means vertex form, so we need $2(x-h)^2+k$.

\emph{Step 1.} $h=-\dfrac{b}{2a}=-\dfrac{-12}{2(2)}=3$.

\emph{Step 2.} $k=f(3)=2(9)-12(3)+13=18-36+13=-5$.

\emph{Step 3.} So $f(x)=2(x-3)^2-5$, and a quick expansion confirms it: $2(x^2-6x+9)-5=2x^2-12x+18-5=2x^2-12x+13$. \checkmark

The minimum value is $-5$, attained at $x=3$. Notice that $-5$ is now sitting in the expression as a constant, which is exactly what the question asked for; in the original form it was invisible.

blocks.title: Three ways students lose this point
blocks.body:
\textbf{1. The sign of $h$.} In $f(x)=(x+6)^2-11$ the vertex is $(-6,-11)$, not $(6,-11)$. Vertex form is $a(x-h)^2+k$, so $x+6$ means $h=-6$. Ask yourself: what value of $x$ makes the squared part zero?

\textbf{2. Answering the wrong coordinate.} ``What is the maximum height?'' wants the $y$-value; ``after how many seconds is the height greatest?'' wants the $x$-value. Both numbers appear in the choices, every time.

\textbf{3. Reading a zero as its negative.} From $g(x)=(x-2)(x+5)$ the $x$-intercepts are $x=2$ and $x=-5$ -- the values that make each factor zero, not the numbers you see written.

blocks.title: Polynomials: zeros, multiplicity and end behaviour
blocks.body:
For a polynomial in factored form, each factor $(x-r)$ contributes a zero at $x=r$. The exponent on that factor is its \textbf{multiplicity}, and multiplicity controls what the graph does there: an odd multiplicity means the graph \emph{crosses} the $x$-axis, an even multiplicity means it \emph{touches} and turns back.

\textbf{End behaviour} depends on only two things, the degree and the sign of the leading coefficient. Odd degree sends the two ends in opposite directions; even degree sends them the same way. A positive leading coefficient sends the right-hand end up, a negative one sends it down. So $p(x)=-2x^3+5x-1$ (odd degree, negative lead) falls to $-\infty$ on the right and rises to $+\infty$ on the left.

blocks.title: The remainder and factor theorems
blocks.body:
\textbf{Remainder theorem.} When a polynomial $p(x)$ is divided by $x-a$, the remainder is $p(a)$. You never have to do long division on the SAT -- substitute.

\textbf{Factor theorem.} $x-a$ is a factor of $p(x)$ exactly when $p(a)=0$; equivalently, $a$ is a zero of $p$ and $(a,0)$ is an $x$-intercept of the graph.

Watch the sign: dividing by $x+3$ means $a=-3$, so evaluate $p(-3)$.

blocks.title: Worked example 2 -- the factor theorem with an unknown
blocks.body:
\textbf{The polynomial $p$ is defined by $p(x)=3x^3-5x^2+kx+8$, where $k$ is a constant. If $x-2$ is a factor of $p(x)$, what is the value of $k$?}

\emph{Step 1.} ``$x-2$ is a factor'' translates, by the factor theorem, into $p(2)=0$. That single translation is the whole question.

\emph{Step 2.} $p(2)=3(8)-5(4)+2k+8=24-20+2k+8=2k+12$.

\emph{Step 3.} Set it equal to zero: $2k+12=0$, so $k=-6$.

Check: with $k=-6$, $p(2)=24-20-12+8=0$. \checkmark\ If the question had instead said ``the remainder is $4$ when $p(x)$ is divided by $x-2$'', the only change would be $2k+12=4$.

blocks.title: On test day
blocks.body:
\textbf{Read the answer choices first} on ``which form displays\dots'' questions. If every choice is factored, the question is about intercepts; if every choice is $a(x-h)^2+k$, it is about the vertex. You then only have to check which one is genuinely equivalent, and expanding a choice is faster than completing the square.

\textbf{Use the graphing calculator for confirmation, not for solving.} Typing the function in and reading the vertex takes about as long as $-\frac{b}{2a}$, but it is an excellent check when a question is worth a full re-read.

\textbf{Underline what is asked} -- ``$x$-coordinate'', ``value of $f$'', ``how many seconds'', ``how high''. The distractors on this topic are built almost entirely from students answering the right question's neighbour.

problems.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=(x-4)^2+7$. What is the vertex of the graph of $y=f(x)$ in the $xy$-plane?
problems.solution: Vertex form is $f(x)=a(x-h)^2+k$ with vertex $(h,k)$. The squared part is zero when $x=4$, which is where the parabola turns, and the value there is $7$. The number inside the parentheses is subtracted, so $x-4$ gives $h=+4$, not $-4$.

problems.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=x^2-6x+11$. The axis of symmetry of the graph of $y=f(x)$ in the $xy$-plane is the line $x=c$. What is the value of $c$?
problems.solution: A parabola is symmetric about the vertical line through its vertex, and the vertex of $ax^2+bx+c$ sits at $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$. With $a=1$ and $b=-6$ that line is $x=3$.

problems.stem: The function $g$ is defined by $g(x)=(x-2)(x+5)$. What are the $x$-intercepts of the graph of $y=g(x)$ in the $xy$-plane?
problems.solution: A product is zero exactly when one of its factors is zero, so set each factor equal to $0$. The intercepts are the values that make the factors vanish, which are the opposites of the numbers you see written: $x-2=0$ gives $x=2$ and $x+5=0$ gives $x=-5$.

problems.stem: What is the $y$-coordinate of the $y$-intercept of the graph of $y=(x-3)(x+8)$ in the $xy$-plane?
problems.solution: Every $y$-intercept is found the same way, in any form: substitute $x=0$. Here $(0-3)(0+8)=-24$. The choice $24$ comes from multiplying $3$ and $8$ without tracking the signs.

problems.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=-(x-1)^2+6$. What is the maximum value of $f(x)$?
problems.solution: Because $(x-1)^2$ is never negative, $-(x-1)^2$ is never positive, so the largest possible output happens when the squared term is $0$, at $x=1$. The value there is $6$. The number $1$ is where the maximum occurs, not the maximum itself.
steps: The greatest value of $f$ occurs when $(x-1)^2=0$, that is at $x=1$.

problems.stem: The remainder when the polynomial $p(x)=x^2+3x-5$ is divided by $x-2$ is $r$. What is the value of $r$?
problems.solution: The remainder theorem replaces division entirely: dividing by $x-a$ leaves the remainder $p(a)$. Here $a=2$, so evaluate $p(2)=4+6-5=5$.
steps: By the remainder theorem the remainder is $p(2)$.
problems.verify:
x = symbols('x')
p = x**2 + 3*x - 5
result = p.subs(x, 2)

problems.stem: In the $xy$-plane, which of the following equations defines a parabola with vertex $(5,-2)$?
problems.solution: Vertex form $y=(x-h)^2+k$ has vertex $(h,k)$, so a vertex of $(5,-2)$ requires $h=5$ and $k=-2$; that is, $x$ minus $5$, then minus $2$ at the end. Writing $x+5$ would place the vertex at $x=-5$, and swapping the two numbers gives the vertex $(2,5)$ instead.

problems.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to $x^2+8x+3$ and displays the minimum value of the function $f(x)=x^2+8x+3$ as a constant or coefficient?
problems.solution: The minimum value is displayed by vertex form, so complete the square: half of $8$ is $4$, and $(x+4)^2=x^2+8x+16$, which overshoots the constant by $16$. Subtracting that gives $(x+4)^2-13$, whose expansion returns the original expression, so the minimum value is $-13$.
steps: Vertex form displays the minimum as the constant $k$.

problems.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=3x^2-12x+7$. What is the $x$-coordinate of the vertex of the graph of $y=f(x)$ in the $xy$-plane?
problems.solution: With a leading coefficient other than $1$ the formula $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$ still applies, but the $2a$ in the denominator matters: $-\frac{-12}{2(3)}=2$. Forgetting the $a$ would give $6$.

problems.stem: A ball is thrown upward from a platform. Its height above the ground, in feet, $t$ seconds after it is thrown is given by $h(t)=-16t^2+64t+5$. What is the maximum height, in feet, reached by the ball?
problems.solution: The greatest height is the $y$-value of the vertex, so first find when it occurs, $t=-\frac{64}{2(-16)}=2$ seconds, then substitute back to get the height itself. The number $2$ is the time, and $5$ is the height at the moment of release, so neither answers the question asked.
steps: The parabola opens downward, so the vertex is the maximum.

problems.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to $x^2-2x-15$ and displays the $x$-intercepts of the graph of $y=x^2-2x-15$ as constants or coefficients?
problems.solution: The $x$-intercepts are displayed by factored form, so look for two numbers multiplying to $-15$ and adding to $-2$: those are $-5$ and $+3$. Expanding $(x+5)(x-3)$ instead gives $x^2+2x-15$, the right constant but the wrong middle term, which is why checking the linear coefficient is the fast way to eliminate.
steps: Look for two numbers with product $-15$ and sum $-2$.
The intercepts $x=5$ and $x=-3$ are now visible.

problems.stem: The polynomial function $p$ is defined by $p(x)=x(x-3)^2(x+4)$. Which zero of $p$ has multiplicity $2$?
problems.solution: The multiplicity of a zero is the exponent on its factor. Only $(x-3)$ is squared, so the zero $x=3$ has multiplicity $2$; the exponent $2$ is not itself a zero, which is the trap in choice C.

problems.stem: The polynomial function $p$ is defined by $p(x)=-2x^3+5x-1$. Which of the following describes the end behaviour of the graph of $y=p(x)$ in the $xy$-plane?
choices: As $x$ increases without bound, $p(x)$ increases without bound; as $x$ decreases without bound, $p(x)$ decreases without bound.
As $x$ increases without bound, $p(x)$ decreases without bound; as $x$ decreases without bound, $p(x)$ increases without bound.
As $x$ increases or decreases without bound, $p(x)$ increases without bound.
As $x$ increases or decreases without bound, $p(x)$ decreases without bound.
problems.solution: End behaviour is decided entirely by the leading term $-2x^3$. The degree $3$ is odd, so the two ends go opposite ways, and the leading coefficient $-2$ is negative, so the right-hand end goes down. The lower-degree terms $5x-1$ are irrelevant once $|x|$ is large.
steps: Odd degree means the ends behave oppositely.
The negative coefficient sends the graph down on the right and up on the left.
problems.verify: result = "As $x$ increases without bound, $p(x)$ decreases without bound; as $x$ decreases without bound, $p(x)$ increases without bound."

problems.stem: Which of the following is a factor of the polynomial $p(x)=x^3-7x+6$?
problems.solution: By the factor theorem, $x-a$ is a factor exactly when $p(a)=0$, so test the candidates rather than dividing. $p(1)=1-7+6=0$, so $x-1$ is a factor; by contrast $p(-1)=-1+7+6=12$ and $p(3)=27-21+6=12$, so those are not.
problems.verify:
x = symbols('x')
zeros = sorted(solve(x**3 - 7*x + 6, x))
result = x - zeros[1]

problems.stem: In the $xy$-plane, the graph of the quadratic function $g$ crosses the $x$-axis at $(1,0)$ and at $(7,0)$. What is the $x$-coordinate of the vertex of the graph of $g$?
problems.solution: A parabola is symmetric, so its two $x$-intercepts are the same distance from the axis of symmetry, and the vertex sits exactly halfway between them. The midpoint of $1$ and $7$ is $\frac{1+7}{2}=4$. Choice C is their difference and choice D their sum, neither of which is a midpoint.
steps: The vertex lies on the axis of symmetry, midway between the $x$-intercepts.

problems.stem: In the $xy$-plane, the graph of the quadratic function $f$ has vertex $(2,-3)$ and passes through the point $(4,5)$. The function can be written as $f(x)=a(x-2)^2-3$, where $a$ is a constant. What is the value of $a$?
problems.solution: The vertex fixes $h$ and $k$; one more point is exactly enough to pin down $a$. Substituting $(4,5)$ gives $a(2)^2-3=5$, so $4a=8$ and $a=2$. Choice D is the value of $4a$, the number you get if you forget to divide.

problems.stem: The polynomial $p$ is defined by $p(x)=2x^3+kx-6$, where $k$ is a constant. When $p(x)$ is divided by $x-2$, the remainder is $4$. What is the value of $k$?
problems.solution: The remainder theorem turns a division statement into a single equation: dividing by $x-2$ leaves $p(2)$, so $p(2)=4$. Expanding gives $16+2k-6=4$, and solving yields $k=-3$.
problems.verify:
k = symbols('k')
result = solve(Eq(2*2**3 + k*2 - 6, 4), k)[0]

problems.figure: \begin{center}\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6.4cm,height=5.2cm,axis lines=middle,xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$},xlabel style={below right},ylabel style={above left},xmin=-4.2,xmax=6.2,ymin=-6.2,ymax=6.2,xtick={-4,-2,2,4,6},ytick={-6,-4,-2,2,4,6},tick label style={font=\tiny},grid=both,grid style={line width=0.1pt,draw=satline},samples=101]\addplot[thick,satblue,domain=-2.05:4.05]{(x-1)^2-4};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}\end{center}
problems.stem: The graph of the quadratic function $f$ is shown in the $xy$-plane above. Which equation could define $f$?
problems.solution: Read the vertex off the picture: it is at $(1,-4)$, so vertex form must be $(x-1)^2-4$. The graph opens upward, which rules out the negative leading coefficient, and the $x$-intercepts at $-1$ and $3$ confirm the choice, since $(x-1)^2-4=(x-3)(x+1)$.
steps: The lowest point of the graph is $(1,-4)$, so $h=1$ and $k=-4$.

problems.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to $(x-3)^2-16$ and displays the $y$-coordinate of the $y$-intercept of the graph of $y=(x-3)^2-16$ as a constant or coefficient?
problems.solution: The $y$-intercept is displayed by standard form, whose constant term is $f(0)$. Expanding, $(x-3)^2-16=x^2-6x+9-16=x^2-6x-7$, so the graph crosses the $y$-axis at $(0,-7)$. Choice A is what you get by expanding the square but forgetting the $-16$.
steps: The constant $-7$ is the $y$-coordinate of the $y$-intercept.

problems.stem: The polynomial $p$ is defined by $p(x)=x^3+ax^2-9x-18$, where $a$ is a constant. If $x+2$ is a factor of $p(x)$, what is the value of $a$?
problems.solution: ``$x+2$ is a factor'' means $p(-2)=0$ -- note the sign, since $x+2=x-(-2)$. Substituting gives $-8+4a+18-18=0$, so $4a=8$ and $a=2$.
steps: Write $x+2$ as $x-(-2)$, so the factor theorem gives $p(-2)=0$.

problems.stem: A store's daily revenue, in dollars, from selling an item at a price of $p$ dollars is modelled by $R(p)=p(120-4p)$. What is the maximum daily revenue, in dollars?
problems.solution: In factored form the zeros of $R$ are $p=0$ and $p=30$, so by symmetry the maximum occurs halfway between, at $p=15$; the revenue there is $15(120-60)=900$. Choice A is the price that produces the maximum, not the revenue, and choice B is the second factor's value.
problems.verify:
p = symbols('p')
R = p*(120 - 4*p)
result = R.subs(p, 15)

problems.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=a(x-3)^2+5$, where $a$ is a negative constant. Which of the following must be true?
choices: The graph of $y=f(x)$ has a minimum at the point $(3,5)$.
The graph of $y=f(x)$ is symmetric about the line $x=5$.
problems.solution: Since $a<0$ the parabola opens downward, so the vertex $(3,5)$ is a maximum and the greatest output is $5$. The axis of symmetry is $x=3$, not $x=5$, and because the vertex lies above the $x$-axis on a downward parabola the graph must in fact cross the $x$-axis twice.
steps: Vertex form gives vertex $(3,5)$ and axis of symmetry $x=3$.
$a<0$ means the parabola opens downward, so the vertex is the highest point.
Therefore the maximum value of $f$ is $5$.

problems.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=-(x+6)^2+11$. For what value of $x$ does $f$ attain its maximum value?
problems.solution: The squared term is subtracted, so $f$ is largest when $(x+6)^2=0$, which happens at $x=-6$. Writing vertex form as $a(x-h)^2+k$ shows $x+6=x-(-6)$, so $h=-6$; the value $11$ is the maximum itself, not where it occurs.

problems.stem: The function $g$ is defined by $g(x)=2x^2-16x+5$. The graph of $y=g(x)$ in the $xy$-plane is symmetric about the line $x=c$. What is the value of $c$?
problems.solution: The line of symmetry passes through the vertex, at $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$. With $a=2$ and $b=-16$ this is $\frac{16}{4}=4$; dividing by $a$ alone rather than $2a$ would wrongly give $8$.

problems.stem: The polynomial function $p$ is defined by $p(x)=x(x-7)(x+2)$. What are the $x$-intercepts of the graph of $y=p(x)$ in the $xy$-plane?
problems.solution: Each factor contributes one zero: $x=0$ from the bare $x$, $x=7$ from $x-7$, and $x=-2$ from $x+2$. Dropping the factor $x$ itself, as in choice C, is the most common slip, since it looks like a coefficient rather than a factor.
steps: Set each factor equal to zero.

problems.stem: What is the remainder when the polynomial $p(x)=x^3-2x^2+5$ is divided by $x+1$?
problems.solution: Dividing by $x+1$ means dividing by $x-(-1)$, so the remainder is $p(-1)=-1-2+5=2$. Evaluating $p(1)=4$ instead -- the sign slip -- is choice C.
problems.verify:
x = symbols('x')
p = x**3 - 2*x**2 + 5
result = p.subs(x, -1)

problems.stem: The function $h$ is defined by $h(x)=3(x-2)^2-5$. What is the $y$-coordinate of the $y$-intercept of the graph of $y=h(x)$ in the $xy$-plane?
problems.solution: The $y$-intercept is always $h(0)$, whatever form the rule is in: $3(0-2)^2-5=3(4)-5=7$. Vertex form does not display the $y$-intercept, so the constant $-5$ is the minimum value, not the intercept.

problems.stem: The polynomial function $q$ is defined by $q(x)=4x^4-x^3+2$. Which of the following describes the end behaviour of the graph of $y=q(x)$ in the $xy$-plane?
choices: As $x$ increases or decreases without bound, $q(x)$ increases without bound.
As $x$ increases or decreases without bound, $q(x)$ decreases without bound.
As $x$ increases without bound, $q(x)$ increases without bound; as $x$ decreases without bound, $q(x)$ decreases without bound.
As $x$ increases without bound, $q(x)$ decreases without bound; as $x$ decreases without bound, $q(x)$ increases without bound.
problems.solution: Only the leading term $4x^4$ matters far from the origin. The degree $4$ is even, so both ends behave the same way, and the coefficient $4$ is positive, so both ends rise. The $-x^3$ term changes the middle of the graph but not its ends.
steps: Even degree means both ends go the same direction.
The positive leading coefficient sends both ends upward.
problems.verify: result = "As $x$ increases or decreases without bound, $q(x)$ increases without bound."

problems.stem: In the $xy$-plane, which of the following equations defines a parabola with $x$-intercepts at $(6,0)$ and $(-1,0)$?
problems.solution: A zero at $x=r$ comes from the factor $x-r$, so intercepts at $6$ and $-1$ require the factors $x-6$ and $x-(-1)=x+1$. Choice A reverses both signs and would give intercepts at $-6$ and $1$.

problems.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=x^2-10x+21$. When $f(x)$ is written in the form $(x-h)^2+k$, where $h$ and $k$ are constants, what is the value of $h+k$?
problems.solution: Half of $-10$ is $-5$, and $(x-5)^2=x^2-10x+25$, which is $4$ too large, so $f(x)=(x-5)^2-4$. That gives $h=5$ and $k=-4$, so $h+k=1$.
problems.verify:
x = symbols('x')
h = Rational(10, 2)
k = (x**2 - 10*x + 21).subs(x, h)
result = h + k

problems.stem: A rocket is launched from a platform. Its height above the ground, in metres, $t$ seconds after launch is given by $h(t)=-5t^2+40t+2$. How many seconds after launch does the rocket reach its greatest height?
problems.solution: The question asks \emph{when}, so it wants the $x$-coordinate of the vertex: $t=-\frac{40}{2(-5)}=4$ seconds. Choice D, $82$, is the greatest height in metres, and choice A is the launch height -- both are numbers in the problem, but neither is a time.
steps: The parabola opens downward, so the vertex gives the greatest height.

problems.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to $2x^2-12x+13$ and displays the minimum value of the function $f(x)=2x^2-12x+13$ as a constant or coefficient?
problems.solution: Vertex form displays the minimum. Here $h=-\frac{-12}{2(2)}=3$ and $k=f(3)=18-36+13=-5$, so the expression is $2(x-3)^2-5$; expanding confirms $2x^2-12x+18-5=2x^2-12x+13$. Choice B uses $b$ itself instead of $-\frac{b}{2a}$ for $h$.

problems.stem: The polynomial function $p$ is defined by $p(x)=(x-1)(x+3)(x+4)$. What is the value of $p(2)$?
problems.solution: Substitute directly into the factored form rather than expanding: $p(2)=(2-1)(2+3)(2+4)=(1)(5)(6)=30$. Choice A comes from mishandling the sign of the first factor as $1-2=-1$.

problems.stem: The polynomial function $p$ is defined by $p(x)=(x+1)^3(x-2)^2$. Which of the following describes the behaviour of the graph of $y=p(x)$ at its $x$-intercepts?
choices: The graph crosses the $x$-axis at $x=-1$ and touches the $x$-axis at $x=2$.
The graph touches the $x$-axis at $x=-1$ and crosses the $x$-axis at $x=2$.
The graph crosses the $x$-axis at both $x=-1$ and $x=2$.
The graph touches the $x$-axis at both $x=-1$ and $x=2$.
problems.solution: Multiplicity decides the behaviour at a zero. The factor $(x+1)$ has odd multiplicity $3$, so the graph passes through the axis at $x=-1$; the factor $(x-2)$ has even multiplicity $2$, so near $x=2$ the sign of $p$ cannot change and the graph touches and turns back.
steps: The zero $x=-1$ has multiplicity $3$, which is odd, so the graph crosses there.
The zero $x=2$ has multiplicity $2$, which is even, so the graph touches there.
problems.verify: result = "The graph crosses the $x$-axis at $x=-1$ and touches the $x$-axis at $x=2$."

problems.stem: The graph of the quadratic function $f$ is shown in the $xy$-plane above. Which equation could define $f$?
problems.solution: The lowest point of the graph is $(-2,-9)$, so vertex form needs $h=-2$ and $k=-9$, and $h=-2$ appears in the equation as $x+2$. The curve opens upward, so the leading coefficient is positive; as a check, the $x$-intercepts $-5$ and $1$ satisfy $(x+2)^2-9=(x+5)(x-1)$.
steps: Read the vertex from the graph: $(-2,-9)$.

problems.stem: In the $xy$-plane, the graph of the quadratic function $f$ crosses the $x$-axis at $(1,0)$ and $(9,0)$, and the minimum value of $f$ is $-32$. The function is defined by $f(x)=a(x-1)(x-9)$, where $a$ is a constant. What is the value of $a$?
problems.solution: The minimum occurs on the axis of symmetry, midway between the intercepts, at $x=5$. Then $f(5)=a(4)(-4)=-16a$, and setting $-16a=-32$ gives $a=2$.

problems.stem: Which of the following is a factor of the polynomial $p(x)=x^3+2x^2-11x-12$?
problems.solution: Test each candidate with the factor theorem instead of dividing. $p(3)=27+18-33-12=0$, so $x-3$ is a factor. The other candidates give $p(2)=-18$, $p(1)=-20$ and $p(-3)=12$, none of which is zero.
steps: For a factor $x-a$, the factor theorem requires $p(a)=0$.
problems.verify:
x = symbols('x')
zeros = sorted(solve(x**3 + 2*x**2 - 11*x - 12, x))
result = x - zeros[2]

problems.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to $2x^2-2x-12$ and displays the $x$-intercepts of the graph of $y=2x^2-2x-12$ as constants or coefficients?
problems.solution: Factor the common $2$ out first: $2x^2-2x-12=2(x^2-x-6)=2(x-3)(x+2)$. Choice A factors correctly but drops the leading $2$, so it is not equivalent to the original expression -- and equivalence is part of what the question demands, even though both would suggest the same intercepts.
steps: So the expression is $2(x-3)(x+2)$, showing intercepts at $x=3$ and $x=-2$.

problems.stem: The polynomial $p$ is defined by $p(x)=3x^3-5x^2+kx+8$, where $k$ is a constant. If $x-2$ is a factor of $p(x)$, what is the value of $k$?
problems.solution: By the factor theorem, $x-2$ being a factor means $p(2)=0$. Evaluating gives $24-20+2k+8=2k+12$, so $2k+12=0$ and $k=-6$.
problems.verify:
k = symbols('k')
result = solve(Eq(3*2**3 - 5*2**2 + k*2 + 8, 0), k)[0]

problems.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=x^2+5x+3$. What is the minimum value of $f(x)$?
problems.solution: The minimum value is the output at the vertex, so first find $x=-\frac{5}{2}$, then substitute: $\frac{25}{4}-\frac{25}{2}+3=-\frac{13}{4}$. Choice C is the $x$-coordinate of the vertex, the classic wrong-coordinate answer on this topic.

problems.stem: In the $xy$-plane, the graph of $y=x^2+bx+c$ has its vertex at $(3,-4)$, where $b$ and $c$ are constants. What is the value of $c$?
problems.solution: Start from the form that shows the vertex, $y=(x-3)^2-4$, then expand into standard form to read off $c$: $x^2-6x+9-4=x^2-6x+5$. Equivalently, $c=f(0)=9-4=5$. Choice A is $b$, and choice B is the $y$-coordinate of the vertex.

problems.stem: A company's daily profit, in dollars, from selling $x$ units of a product is modelled by $P(x)=-2x^2+56x-180$. What is the maximum daily profit, in dollars?
problems.solution: The parabola opens downward, so the maximum profit is the value at the vertex. It occurs at $x=-\frac{56}{2(-2)}=14$ units, and $P(14)=-392+784-180=212$ dollars. Stopping at $14$ answers ``how many units'', not ``how much profit''.

problems.stem: The polynomial function $p$ is defined by $p(x)=-(x-1)^2(x+3)$. Which of the following statements about the graph of $y=p(x)$ in the $xy$-plane is true?
choices: The graph touches the $x$-axis at $x=1$, and $p(x)$ decreases without bound as $x$ increases without bound.
The graph crosses the $x$-axis at $x=1$, and $p(x)$ increases without bound as $x$ increases without bound.
The graph touches the $x$-axis at $x=-3$, and $p(x)$ decreases without bound as $x$ increases without bound.
The graph touches the $x$-axis at $x=1$, and $p(x)$ increases without bound as $x$ increases without bound.
problems.solution: Two independent readings are needed. The factor $(x-1)^2$ has even multiplicity, so the graph touches the axis at $x=1$, while $(x+3)$ has multiplicity $1$, so it crosses at $x=-3$. Expanding mentally, the leading term is $-x^3$: odd degree with a negative coefficient, so the right-hand end falls.
steps: $(x-1)^2$ has even multiplicity, so the graph touches at $x=1$.
The degree is $2+1=3$ and the leading coefficient is $-1$.
Odd degree with a negative lead means $p(x)$ falls without bound as $x$ grows.
problems.verify: result = "The graph touches the $x$-axis at $x=1$, and $p(x)$ decreases without bound as $x$ increases without bound."

problems.stem: The polynomial $p$ is defined by $p(x)=x^3-6x^2+11x-6$. If $p(x)=(x-3)q(x)$ for some polynomial $q$, which of the following is the expression $q(x)$?
problems.solution: Because $p(3)=27-54+33-6=0$, the factor $x-3$ does divide $p$, and the quotient must be a quadratic $x^2+mx+2$: its leading coefficient is $1$ to reproduce $x^3$, and its constant term must satisfy $(-3)(\text{constant})=-6$, so the constant is $2$. Matching the $x^2$ term, $m-3=-6$ gives $m=-3$, so $q(x)=x^2-3x+2$.
steps: The quotient is quadratic with leading coefficient $1$ and constant $\frac{-6}{-3}=2$.
